Issued at 313 PM EST Thu Nov 26 2026

Pattern Synopsis/Forecast: Split flow pattern across eastern North 
America this Thanksgiving Day afternoon...with a nice upper low 
having been carved out in the southern branch flow over the 
middle/lower Mississippi Valley.  Active Pacific wave train farther 
upstream...an initial short wave trough got caught in the northern 
branch flow and is now crossing Manitoba/northwest Ontario; second 
short wave trough crashing onshore today over the Pacific Northwest/ 
British Columbia.  East-west oriented narrow ridge axis to the north 
of the southern branch low extends from New England back across the 
Lake Superior basin...setting up a bit of a deformation zone and a 
tightening moisture gradient pushing into southern Lower.  At the 
surface...anomalous (+2 to +3 sigma) 1043mb high over New England 
ridging back into the upper Midwest...with a tightening pressure 
graident between it and deepening (998mb) low pressure crawling up 
the east coast.  

Southern branch upper low forecast track across the lower Lakes and 
New England over the next 48 hours...as larger scale pattern trends 
toward mean long wave troughing across the eastern half of North 
America at least to start next week.  But eventually a more zonal 
Pacific-dominant pattern evolves by midweek (i.e., not cold).  In 
the shorter term...interesting evolution of east coast low over the 
next day or so.  Initial coastal low attached to an earlier piece of 
southern branch energy that got kicked eastward by the developing 
larger low over the lower Mississippi Valley.  Eventually this lead 
wave lifts northward faster than its surface reflection...so the 
initial east coast low weakens and a second forms farther inland in 
response to the main upper low that will be lifting northeast toward 
the lower Lakes later today.  The result is a new surface low Friday 
morning over western Pennsylvania/New York...and a decent cyclonic 
gradient lashing the upper Great Lakes Friday.  Once this system 
lifts out Friday night...remnants of energy impacting the Pacific 
Northwest today expected to slide across Michigan Saturday.  This 
will be followed by a stronger split short wave trough Sunday... 
southern branch wave induces cyclogenesis to the less of the 
southern Rockies Saturday.  This system will track south of 
Michigan...with but will bring an increased threat for precipitation 
Sunday and a quick push of colder air to start the week.

Primary Forecast Concerns:  

Impacts of low pressure lifting northeast across the lower Great 
Lakes/New England through Saturday: First order of business is 
northern/western extent of precipitation shield spreading northwest 
across southern Lower this afternoon...along with pushing a thick Cs 
overcast across northern Michigan.  Leading edge of the rain should 
be on the doorstep of Saginaw Bay by early evening...though northern 
edge may have to fight downward branch of low level frontogenetic 
circulation. Eventually northwest edge of precipitation band 
probably ends up roughly along an MBL-PZQ line by Sunday morning... 
and a little bit of a virga storm north of that. And that may be the 
westward extent of the precipitation threat as the back edge of the 
rain shield starts to pivot Sunday morning and pulls east during the 
afternoon. Precipitation type expected to be mostly rain...some 
marginal chances for snow or a mix across the higher terrain of 
northern Lower.  Winds will remain gusty from the northeast 
tonight...backing to the north Friday before diminishing. 

Some showers Saturday??:  Quick moving negatively tilted short wave 
trough swings across Michigan Saturday expected to bring some 
showers to the area.  Have bumped up PoPs from the consensus... 
though they were a bit lacking...but with just light rainfall 
amounts respected.   

More widespread precipitation Sunday along with a quick shot of 
colder air Monday:  Next system will track along/north of the Ohio 
River Sunday...but looks to have an extensive deformation zone 
precipitation shield that extends up into Lower Michigan.  Rain 
spreads across northern Lower Michigan and probably far eastern 
Upper Sunday morning...then shifts east Sunday evening (could see 
some snow on the backside of the precipitation shield as it pulls 
away).  Low level cold advection sets in overnight Sunday into 
Monday morning...850mb temperatures dropping toward -8C expected to 
result in a transition to lake effect snow showers in northwest 
flow.
